label: last copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively on the final output step (to_go==0). For L=3 (t=5, outputting the 3rd original token while the 2nd is input) it fires on ~94% of sequences and carries ~91% of activation mass. A weak tail fires on the final step of L=4 sequences (t=7, ~6% of them, ~8% of mass, mostly low-quartile magnitudes). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, on first occurrences of the input token, or for L>=5. Magnitude: strongest examples have first token q (or a) with input b/v/u/p/m; the L=4 tail is weak.

issues: All factual claims hold on dev: active only in the copy phase (100% of mass). to_go==0 holds 99.8% of mass. L=3 fires on 2456 of about 2605 sequences (about 94%) and holds 91.5% of mass. L=4 holds 8.5% of mass at about 6% precision. L>=5 has 25 active steps. Activity is zero when in_first==1. Adding L<=4 gives P 0.193 / R 0.983, matching the explanation.
Test confirmed: P 0.948, R 0.737, F1 0.829, mass recall 0.918.

The recall gap is the low-magnitude L=4 last-step tail (881 test steps, 8.2% of mass, mostly the lowest quartile: quartile coverage 0.26/0.72/0.97/1.0). I found no separable subclass. Restricting L=4 by in_tok in {v,p,b,k} gives at best P 0.26, and adding first-token or prev-token filters gives P up to 0.58 but recall of only about 0.04. None of these would raise F1 meaningfully.

The 136 test false positives on L=3 look like scattered token-dependent weak cases. Excluding some first tokens (h,r,w,i,3) barely raises precision (0.954) and costs recall, so this is not a systematic class.
Minor: the label 'last copy step of length-3 sequences' leaves out the weak L=4 tail, which the explanation does acknowledge.

Mismatch with the user's request: the user asked to run the baseline on the 1/5-subsampled data in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but this check used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store as the computed task instructed. I did not confirm whether that store was built from the subsampled data.
